scenarios.title: M0 · Normal Sinus
scenarios.description: Maintain VVI standby pacing while observing intrinsic beats.

alarm.text: No active alarms

scenarios.objective: Confirm the pacemaker remains inhibited while the patient maintains an intrinsic sinus rate.
scenarios.feedback: No pacing spikes should be visible. If pacing occurs, lower the rate below the intrinsic rhythm or verify sensing leads.

scenarios.title: M1 · Symptomatic Bradycardia
scenarios.description: Patient with symptomatic ventricular bradycardia requiring VVI demand pacing.

alarm.text: Symptomatic bradycardia – initiate pacing

scenarios.objective: Increase the VVI pacing rate above the intrinsic 34–38 ppm rhythm with adequate output and sensitivity to achieve consistent ventricular capture.
scenarios.feedback: Start VVI pacing, set the rate to 60–70 ppm, output to 5–10 mA, and sensitivity around 2 mV to obtain paced QRS complexes.

rules.description: Loss of capture when pacing output is inadequate despite the higher rate.

alarm.text: Loss of capture – increase output

effects.feedback: Raise the output to at least 5 mA and reassess capture at the paced rate.

rules.description: Oversensing inhibits pacing when sensitivity is set too low (too sensitive).

alarm.text: Oversensing – decrease sensitivity (raise mV)

effects.feedback: Reduce sensitivity toward ~2 mV so that only true R-waves are sensed and pacing is not inappropriately inhibited.

rules.description: Stable ventricular capture once rate, output, and sensitivity are set appropriately.

alarm.text: Capture achieved – maintain VVI pacing

effects.feedback: Paced rhythm should be stable at the selected rate with each pacing spike followed by a QRS complex and improved blood pressure.

scenarios.title: M2 · Capture Threshold Test
scenarios.description: Determine the ventricular capture threshold and program an appropriate safety margin.

alarm.text: Begin threshold test – rate above intrinsic

scenarios.objective: Increase the VVI rate above the intrinsic rhythm, slowly reduce the output to find the minimal output that consistently captures, then program a final output with a 2–3× safety margin.
scenarios.feedback: Set the rate to ≥70 ppm, decrease output until capture is lost, then increase until every spike captures. Use that value as the threshold and set the final output about 2–3× higher.

rules.description: During the threshold search, output is too low and capture is lost.

alarm.text: Loss of capture – slowly increase output

effects.feedback: You are below the capture threshold. Increase the output in small steps until each pacing spike is followed by a QRS complex.

rules.description: Output is set at the threshold with no safety margin.

alarm.text: Output at threshold – add safety margin

effects.feedback: You have found the capture threshold, but the output should be increased to about 2–3× this value to ensure long-term capture.

rules.description: Stable capture with appropriate safety margin programmed.

alarm.text: Stable capture – threshold and margin set

effects.feedback: All beats are paced at the programmed rate and each spike results in a QRS complex. The programmed output provides an adequate safety margin above the threshold.

scenarios.title: M3 · Sensing & Undersensing
scenarios.description: Determine the ventricular sensing threshold and correct undersensing.
scenarios.primaryRhythm: Intrinsic sinus rhythm with intermittent pacing

alarm.text: Set rate below intrinsic and minimize output

scenarios.objective: With the rate set below the intrinsic rhythm and output minimized, adjust the Sensitivity to find the sensing threshold, recognize undersensing, and program a safe sensitivity setting.
scenarios.feedback: Set the rate at 40–60 ppm and the output very low (e.g. 0.1–1 mA). Adjust sensitivity so that intrinsic R-waves are reliably sensed and pacing is inhibited whenever an intrinsic QRS is present.

rules.description: Undersensing: pacemaker paces despite intrinsic QRS complexes because sensitivity (mV) is set too high (too insensitive).

alarm.text: Undersensing – increase sensitivity (lower mV)

effects.feedback: You see pacing spikes falling on top of intrinsic QRS complexes, and the SENSE indicator is not flashing reliably. Decrease the mV setting to increase sensitivity until all R-waves are detected.

rules.description: Intrinsic rhythm is reliably sensed and pacing is appropriately inhibited.

alarm.text: Sensing threshold set – pacing appropriately inhibited

effects.feedback: The SENSE indicator flashes with each intrinsic QRS, and pacing is inhibited whenever an intrinsic beat occurs. The sensitivity setting is within a safe range.

scenarios.title: M4 · Oversensing & Inhibition
scenarios.description: Recognize oversensing that leads to inappropriate inhibition of pacing and correct it.

alarm.text: Oversensing – long pauses due to pacing inhibition

scenarios.objective: Identify oversensing (e.g. T-waves, noise, far-field signals) that inappropriately inhibits pacing and correct it by decreasing sensitivity (raising mV) without causing undersensing.
scenarios.feedback: When the sensitivity is set too low (very small mV), the SENSE indicator responds to noise or T-waves and pacing is inhibited, causing pauses. Raise the mV setting until only true R-waves are sensed and pacing resumes when needed.

rules.description: Oversensing due to excessively high sensitivity (low mV) leading to bradycardic pauses.

alarm.text: Oversensing – pacing inappropriately inhibited

effects.feedback: Frequent SENSE flashes occur without true QRS complexes, and pacing spikes are inhibited, producing long pauses. Increase the mV setting until oversensing disappears.

rules.description: Oversensing corrected, pacing now appropriately supports the patient without undersensing.

alarm.text: Oversensing corrected – pacing appropriate

effects.feedback: The SENSE indicator corresponds to real QRS complexes only, and pacing occurs when intrinsic beats are absent. Heart rate and blood pressure improve.

scenarios.title: M5 · Threshold Drift & LOC
scenarios.description: Recognize evolving loss of capture and readjust output after threshold drift or lead-related changes.
scenarios.summaryLabel: Threshold drift and loss of capture
scenarios.primaryRhythm: Ventricular pacing with evolving loss of capture

alarm.text: Intermittent loss of capture – reassess threshold

scenarios.objective: Identify intermittent loss of capture due to increased capture threshold or lead issues, reassess the capture threshold, and increase output to restore stable capture.
scenarios.feedback: Previously stable pacing is now intermittently failing. Repeat a capture threshold test and increase the output to restore consistent capture, recognizing that thresholds can change over time.

rules.description: Output has fallen well below the new threshold, leading to complete loss of capture.

alarm.text: Complete loss of capture – increase output immediately

effects.feedback: No QRS complexes follow pacing spikes. Increase the output and reassess the capture threshold. Consider lead position if very high outputs are required.

rules.description: Output is close to the new threshold, causing intermittent loss of capture.

alarm.text: Intermittent capture – increase safety margin

effects.feedback: Some pacing spikes capture while others do not. Increase the output to re-establish a 2–3× safety margin above the new threshold.

rules.description: Output adequately increased, capture restored with safety margin.

alarm.text: Stable capture – monitor for further changes

effects.feedback: All pacing spikes now result in QRS complexes again. Monitor for further threshold changes and consider lead evaluation if unusually high outputs are required.

scenarios.title: M6 · PVCs & PACs in VVI
scenarios.description: Recognize PVCs and PACs on the ECG during VVI pacing and understand their interaction with pacemaker timing.
scenarios.primaryRhythm: Ventricular pacing with PVCs and PACs

alarm.text: Isolated PVCs and PACs – observe

scenarios.objective: Identify PVCs and PACs on a paced ECG strip and explain how these ectopic beats reset or inhibit ventricular pacing without mistaking them for pacemaker malfunction.
scenarios.feedback: With appropriate VVI settings, you should see a paced rhythm interrupted by occasional PVCs and PACs. Recognize their morphology and timing effects without changing pacemaker parameters unnecessarily.

rules.description: Pacemaker appropriately programmed; ectopy is present but device function is normal.

alarm.text: Ectopy present – pacemaker function normal

effects.feedback: You observe paced beats with occasional PVCs and PACs. The timing of pacing spikes adapts to sensed beats as expected; no parameter changes are required.

scenarios.title: M7 · Wide vs Narrow QRS
scenarios.description: Differentiate intrinsic narrow QRS complexes from wide QRS paced beats and PVCs.

alarm.text: Interpret QRS morphology – no immediate intervention

scenarios.objective: Distinguish intrinsic narrow QRS complexes from wide QRS paced beats and PVCs on the ECG, and understand that a wide QRS is expected for ventricular pacing.
scenarios.feedback: Identify which complexes are intrinsic (narrow QRS), which represent ventricular-paced beats (wide QRS following pacing spikes), and which are PVCs (wide, premature beats without preceding pacing spikes). Do not misinterpret normal paced QRS morphology as a pacemaker malfunction.

rules.description: Pacemaker programmed appropriately; scenario focuses on ECG interpretation rather than parameter adjustment.

alarm.text: Parameters acceptable – focus on morphology

effects.feedback: Pacemaker parameters are within normal ranges. Focus on distinguishing intrinsic narrow QRS, paced wide QRS, and PVCs based on morphology and the presence or absence of pacing spikes.

scenarios.title: C1 · Third-degree AV Block
scenarios.description: Placeholder clinical case that mirrors a complete heart block with minimal prompts.

alarm.text: Complete heart block – stabilise the patient

scenarios.objective: Stabilise a patient with complete heart block by establishing reliable ventricular pacing and improving perfusion.
scenarios.feedback: Look for dissociated P waves with a slow ventricular escape rhythm. Initiate pacing with adequate rate and output, then reassess perfusion.

scenarios.title: C2 · Second-degree AV Block (Mobitz II)
scenarios.description: Intermittent non-conducted P waves with sudden dropped QRS complexes; placeholder waveform until precise pattern is added.
scenarios.summaryLabel: Mobitz II with intermittent ventricular pauses

alarm.text: Mobitz II block – anticipate progression

scenarios.objective: Recognise intermittent non-conducted P waves that create sudden ventricular pauses and be ready to support perfusion with pacing.
scenarios.feedback: Note the constant PR intervals with unexpected dropped QRS complexes. Prepare to initiate pacing if perfusion worsens or pauses lengthen.

scenarios.title: C3 · Sick Sinus Syndrome
scenarios.description: Sinus node dysfunction with inappropriate bradycardia and pauses; waveform will be refined later.
scenarios.summaryLabel: Sinus node dysfunction with long pauses

alarm.text: Sinus pauses – evaluate for pacing support

scenarios.objective: Evaluate symptomatic bradycardia from sinus pauses and initiate pacing to maintain cardiac output as needed.
scenarios.feedback: Identify prolonged sinus pauses with slow escape beats. Consider atrial or dual-chamber pacing to prevent perfusion drops.

scenarios.title: C4 · Slow Conduction
scenarios.description: Markedly delayed atrioventricular conduction leading to low ventricular rates; waveform placeholder pending precise trace.
scenarios.summaryLabel: Slow conduction with low ventricular response

alarm.text: Slow ventricular response

scenarios.objective: Manage a patient with markedly delayed conduction by optimising pacing support if the slow ventricular response compromises perfusion.
scenarios.feedback: Watch for very prolonged conduction times and low ventricular rates. Increase pacing support to maintain adequate cardiac output if symptoms emerge.

scenarios.title: M8 · Random Mode
scenarios.description: Mixed scenario that combines elements of all previous cases with randomised rhythm, sensing, and capture patterns.
scenarios.primaryRhythm: Mixed intrinsic, paced, and ectopic beats

alarm.text: Randomised case – identify the main issue

scenarios.objective: Integrate all pacing skills to decide whether pacing is appropriate or malfunctioning and determine the correct intervention, or recognize when no change is needed.
scenarios.feedback: Start by interpreting the ECG and the behaviour of the PACE and SENSE indicators. Adjust rate, output, and sensitivity only when there is clear evidence of undersensing, oversensing, or loss of capture. This scenario is intentionally open-ended.
